records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹֽנִי־צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם כִּֽי־לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת־הָעַי֮ וַיַּחֲרִימָהּ֒ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה לִֽירִיחוֹ֙ וּלְמַלְכָּ֔הּ כֵּן־עָשָׂ֥ה לָעַ֖י וּלְמַלְכָּ֑הּ וְכִ֨י הִשְׁלִ֜ימוּ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י גִבְעוֹן֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ בְּקִרְבָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem that had captured Joshua the Ai and had devoted it to destruction, as he had done to Jericho and to its king so he had done to the Ai and to its king, and that had made peace [the] inhabitants of Gibeon with Israel and were in their midst,
pieces: News reached Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem that Joshua had taken Ai and devoted it to destruction, treating Ai and its king as he had treated Jericho and its king. He also learned that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were now living among them,

L.1: And it happened, when Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and had devoted it to destruction, that as he had done to Jericho and to its king, so he had done to Ai and to its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were in their midst,

R.1: Adoni-Zedek was the king of Jerusalem. He heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Joshua had done to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king. Adoni-Zedek also heard that the people of Gibeon had made a peace treaty with Israel and now lived among the Israelites.

decisions.choice: Adoni-Zedek: a king's name meaning "my lord is righteous" or "my lord is Zedek"
alternatives: my lord is Zedek (a god's name)
decisions.reason: The name joins the word for "lord" with the word for righteousness, which may also be the name of a god. It recalls Melchizedek, "king of righteousness", the king of Salem in Abraham's day (Genesis 14:18). Jerusalem was still a Jebusite city (15:63).

decisions.choice: devoted it to destruction: Ai and its people were given over to God completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for a "devoted thing" (Leviticus 27:28-29). Jericho was devoted to the LORD in this way (6:17, 21), and so was Ai (8:26), though at Ai the livestock and goods were kept as God allowed (8:2, 27).

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel: the treaty of chapter 9
decisions.reason: The Gibeonites tricked Israel into a treaty (9:3-15) and were allowed to live among Israel as its servants (9:26-27). "In their midst" means they now lived as part of Israel, protected by the oath.

decisions.choice: destroyed it completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 2:10 and Deuteronomy 2:34: Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words; Literal and Balanced keep "devote to destruction".

decisions.choice: two (Balanced) or four (Readable) sentences
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is one long clause of what the king heard, which runs into verse 2. Balanced and Readable divide it and repeat "he heard" before the second report.

records.heading: Five kings attack Gibeon

records.source: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י עִ֤יר גְּדוֹלָה֙ גִּבְע֔וֹן כְּאַחַ֖ת עָרֵ֣י הַמַּמְלָכָ֑ה וְכִ֨י הִ֤יא גְדוֹלָה֙ מִן־הָעַ֔י וְכָל־אֲנָשֶׁ֖יהָ גִּבֹּרִֽים׃
records.gloss: and they feared greatly, for a city great [was] Gibeon, like one of [the] cities of the kingdom, and for it [was] greater than the Ai, and all its men [were] warriors.
pieces: he and his people were terrified, because Gibeon was an important city, like one of the royal cities; it was bigger than Ai, and its men were all warriors.

L.2: that they feared greatly, because Gibeon [was] a great city, like one of the cities of the kingdom, and because it [was] greater than Ai, and all its men [were] mighty men.

R.2: He and his people were terrified. Gibeon was a big city, as important as a city ruled by a king. It was bigger than Ai, and all its men were strong fighters.

decisions.choice: they feared: the king and his people
decisions.reason: The verb is plural although verse 1 names only the king. The fear belongs to Adoni-Zedek and the people of Jerusalem together, as Rahab said all Canaan feared Israel (2:9-11).

decisions.choice: like one of the royal cities: a city as strong as those that had their own king
decisions.reason: Gibeon is not said to have had a king; its elders speak for it (9:11). It was still as large and strong as a city that was the seat of a king, so its going over to Israel was a serious loss to the kings of the region.

decisions.choice: mighty men: warriors, men able in battle
decisions.reason: The word describes strong fighting men (6:2). Gibeon had not made peace because it was weak.

decisions.choice: he and his people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are, because the sentence began with the king alone (m1).

decisions.choice: as important as a city ruled by a king
decisions.reason: Readable explains "royal cities" in plain words.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אֲדֹנִי־צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶל־הוֹהָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶ֠בְרוֹן וְאֶל־פִּרְאָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יַרְמ֜וּת וְאֶל־יָפִ֧יעַ מֶֽלֶךְ־לָכִ֛ישׁ וְאֶל־דְּבִ֥יר מֶֽלֶךְ־עֶגְל֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And sent Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem to Hoham king of Hebron and to Piram king of Jarmuth and to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,
pieces: So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent this message to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish and Debir king of Eglon:

L.3: And Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron and to Piram king of Jarmuth and to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,

R.3: So Adoni-Zedek sent messengers to four other kings: Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon. He told them,

decisions.choice: Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, Eglon: cities south and southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Hebron lies in the hills to the south; Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon lie in the low hills to the southwest. Here Debir is the name of the king of Eglon, not the town of Debir taken in verses 38-39.

decisions.choice: sent messengers to four other kings
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "sent to"; Readable says how a king sent word and counts the kings for the reader.

records.source: עֲלֽוּ־אֵלַ֣י וְעִזְרֻ֔נִי וְנַכֶּ֖ה אֶת־גִּבְע֑וֹן כִּֽי־הִשְׁלִ֥ימָה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: "Come up and help me, and let us attack Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

L.4: "Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."

R.4: "Come and help me attack Gibeon, because its people have made peace with Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

decisions.choice: strike: attack in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or hit and is used for attacking and defeating an enemy (verses 10, 20).

decisions.choice: it has made peace: the city stands for its people
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine singular, agreeing with the city. By making peace with Israel, Gibeon had become an enemy of the kings around it.

decisions.choice: its people
decisions.reason: Readable says that the people of the city made the treaty.

records.source: וַיֵּאָסְפ֨וּ וַֽיַּעֲל֜וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת׀מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֗י מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶבְר֤וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־יַרְמוּת֙ מֶֽלֶךְ־לָכִ֣ישׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־עֶגְל֔וֹן הֵ֖ם וְכָל־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ עַל־גִּבְע֔וֹן וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And gathered and went up five kings of the Amorite, king of Jerusalem, king of Hebron, king of Jarmuth, king of Lachish, king of Eglon, they and all their camps, and encamped against Gibeon and fought against it.
pieces: Then the five Amorite kings, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon, joined forces. They went up with all their armies, camped against Gibeon and attacked it.

L.5: And the five kings of the Amorites gathered and went up, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon, they and all their camps, and they camped against Gibeon and made war against it.

R.5: So the five Amorite kings joined together: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon. They marched out with all their armies. They set up camp around Gibeon and attacked it.

decisions.choice: the Amorites: the peoples of the hill country
decisions.reason: "Amorite" is used for the peoples of the hill country of Canaan in general (verse 6; Deuteronomy 1:7, 19-20). The Gibeonites themselves are called Hivites (9:7).

decisions.choice: all their camps: their armies, the forces in the field
decisions.reason: A "camp" is an army on the march or encamped; the plural means the separate forces of the five kings.

decisions.choice: armies
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "camps"; Balanced and Readable name what the camps were.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ גִבְע֨וֹן אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֣לָה לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־תֶּ֥רֶף יָדֶ֖יךָ מֵֽעֲבָדֶ֑יךָ עֲלֵ֧ה אֵלֵ֣ינוּ מְהֵרָ֗ה וְהוֹשִׁ֤יעָה לָּ֨נוּ֙ וְעָזְרֵ֔נוּ כִּ֚י נִקְבְּצ֣וּ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ כָּל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֱמֹרִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And sent [the] men of Gibeon to Joshua to the camp at Gilgal, saying, Do not let drop your hands from your slaves; come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for have gathered against us all [the] kings of the Amorite dwelling [in] the hill country.
pieces: The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants! Come up to us quickly. Rescue us and help us, because all the Amorite kings of the hill country have joined forces against us."

L.6: And the men of Gibeon sent to Joshua, to the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not let your hands drop from your slaves. Come up to us quickly, and save us and help us, because all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."

R.6: The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal. They said, "Do not leave us, your servants, without help! Come quickly and save us. All the Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together to attack us."

decisions.choice: do not let your hands drop from: do not abandon, do not withdraw your support
decisions.reason: To let the hands drop is to let go, to stop holding on to someone or something (Deuteronomy 31:6, 8, "he will not let you go").

decisions.choice: your slaves: the Gibeonites as Israel's bound servants under the treaty
decisions.reason: They had called themselves Joshua's servants (9:8, 11), and Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for Israel (9:23, 27). Now they call on their master to protect them.

decisions.choice: the hill country: the central highlands
decisions.reason: The ridge of hills running north and south through the land, where Jerusalem, Hebron and Gibeon stand. Gilgal lay far below, near the Jordan (4:19).

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal), servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for this word: Literal keeps its hard edge; Balanced and Readable say "servants". Their position is described in m2.

decisions.choice: Do not abandon (Balanced) / Do not leave us ... without help (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m1).

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ מִן־הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל ה֚וּא וְכָל־עַ֤ם הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י הֶחָֽיִל׃פ
records.gloss: And went up Joshua from the Gilgal, he and all [the] people of the war with him and all [the] mighty men of the strength.
pieces: So Joshua went up from Gilgal with his whole army, including all his best fighting men.

L.7: And Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.

R.7: So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with his whole army, including all his best soldiers.

decisions.choice: and all the mighty men of valor: the best warriors within the army
alternatives: a second name for the whole army
decisions.reason: The second phrase may single out the strongest fighters within the whole fighting force, as in 8:3, or it may be a second name for the same army.

decisions.choice: went up: the long climb from the Jordan valley into the hills
decisions.reason: Gilgal lay near Jericho in the Jordan valley, far below Gibeon in the hills; the march meant a steep climb over many miles.

decisions.choice: his whole army
decisions.reason: "All the people of war" means all the fighting men; Balanced and Readable say "army".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י בְיָדְךָ֖ נְתַתִּ֑ים לֹֽא־יַעֲמֹ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ מֵהֶ֖ם בְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, Do not fear them, for into your hand I have given them; not will stand a man of them before you.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. I have handed them over to you. Not one of them will be able to stand against you."

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand. Not a man of them will stand before you."

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. I have already handed them over to you. Not one of them will be able to stop you."

decisions.choice: I have given them: the victory is as good as done
decisions.reason: God speaks of the battle as already decided, before it begins, as at Jericho (6:2) and Ai (8:1).

decisions.choice: into your hand: into your power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control.

decisions.choice: not a man of them will stand before you: the promise of 1:5
decisions.reason: God promised Joshua that no one would be able to stand before him all his life (1:5; Deuteronomy 7:24).

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: Readable adds "already" to show that God speaks of the victory as settled (m1).

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} fights for Israel

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ פִּתְאֹ֑ם כָּל־הַלַּ֕יְלָה עָלָ֖ה מִן־הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃
records.gloss: And came to them Joshua suddenly; all the night he had gone up from the Gilgal.
pieces: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and came upon them by surprise.

L.9: And Joshua came upon them suddenly; all night he had gone up from Gilgal.

R.9: Joshua and his army marched all night from Gilgal and attacked them by surprise.

decisions.choice: all night he had gone up: the night march explains the surprise
decisions.reason: The second clause gives the background of the first: because Joshua climbed through the night, he reached the enemy before they expected him.

decisions.choice: marched all night ... and came upon them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the night march first, in the order things happened.

decisions.choice: and his army ... attacked them
decisions.reason: Readable says that the army went with Joshua (verse 7) and that "came upon them" means he attacked.

records.source: וַיְהֻמֵּ֤ם יְהוָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּכֵּ֥ם מַכָּֽה־גְדוֹלָ֖ה בְּגִבְע֑וֹן וַֽיִּרְדְּפֵ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ מַעֲלֵ֣ה בֵית־חוֹרֹ֔ן וַיַּכֵּ֥ם עַד־עֲזֵקָ֖ה וְעַד־מַקֵּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And threw into panic them Yahweh before Israel, and struck them [a] striking great at Gibeon, and pursued them [by the] way of [the] ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and as far as Makkedah.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} threw them into panic before Israel and struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon. He chased them along the road that climbs to Beth-horon and struck them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw them into panic before Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck them [with] a great striking at Gibeon, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and as far as Makkedah.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the Amorites panic when they faced Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck them down at Gibeon in a great defeat. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chased them along the road up to Beth-horon and struck them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

decisions.choice: threw into panic: the terror and confusion God sends on an enemy
decisions.reason: The verb is used when God throws an army into confusion so that it breaks and runs (Exodus 14:24; Judges 4:15; 1 Samuel 7:10).

decisions.choice: he struck ... pursued ... struck: the LORD is the subject, acting through Israel's army
alternatives: Israel (or Joshua) struck them and pursued them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name a new subject after "the LORD", so the verbs that follow are his. The chapter says the LORD fought for Israel (verses 14, 42), while Israel's soldiers did the fighting with the sword (verse 11). The verbs may also be read with Joshua or Israel as their subject.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Beth-horon, Azekah, Makkedah: the line of the flight
decisions.reason: The road ran west from Gibeon up to Beth-horon and down from the hills (verse 11). Azekah and Makkedah lie in the low hills to the southwest.

decisions.choice: the Amorites ... when they faced Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemy and explains "before Israel". It repeats "the LORD" to show who chased them (m2).

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י בְּנֻסָ֣ם׀מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הֵ֞ם בְּמוֹרַ֤ד בֵּית־חוֹרֹן֙ וַֽיהוָ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֧וֹת מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם עַד־עֲזֵקָ֖ה וַיָּמֻ֑תוּ רַבִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־מֵ֨תוּ֙ בְּאַבְנֵ֣י הַבָּרָ֔ד מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרְג֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ס
records.gloss: And it was, as they fled from before Israel, they [were] on [the] descent of Beth-horon, and Yahweh threw on them stones great from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died; more [were those] who died by [the] stones of the hail than [those] whom killed [the] sons of Israel with the sword.
pieces: As they fled before Israel down the slope from Beth-horon, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hurled huge stones on them from the sky all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hailstones than the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} killed with the sword.

L.11: And it happened, as they fled before Israel, [while] they [were] on the descent of Beth-horon, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw large stones on them from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died. More [were] those who died by the stones of the hail than those whom the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel killed with the sword.

R.11: As the Amorites ran from Israel down the road from Beth-horon, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw huge hailstones down on them from the sky all the way to Azekah. More of them were killed by the hail than by the swords of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: large stones from the heavens: hailstones
decisions.reason: The same stones are called "stones of the hail" in the second half of the verse. God used hail against Egypt too (Exodus 9:23-25), and hail is among his weapons in Job 38:22-23 and Psalm 18:13-14.

decisions.choice: more died by the hail than by the sword: the victory was the LORD's
decisions.reason: The count shows that God, more than Israel's army, won the battle, as verse 14 says: the LORD fought for Israel.

decisions.choice: hailstones
decisions.reason: Readable says at once what the stones were (m1), and names the Amorites as those who fled.

records.source: אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּי֗וֹם תֵּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לְעֵינֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שֶׁ֚מֶשׁ בְּגִבְע֣וֹן דּ֔וֹם וְיָרֵ֖חַ בְּעֵ֥מֶק אַיָּלֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Then spoke Joshua to Yahweh on [the] day [of] giving Yahweh the Amorite before [the] sons of Israel, and he said in [the] eyes of Israel, Sun, at Gibeon be still, and moon, in [the] valley of Aijalon.
pieces: On the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the Amorites up to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, Joshua spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q In full view of Israel he said, \q "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, \q and moon, in the valley of Aijalon!"

L.12: Then Joshua spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the Amorites over before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, \q and he said in the sight of Israel, \q "Sun, at Gibeon be still, \q and moon, in the valley of Aijalon."

R.12: On the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} victory over the Amorites, Joshua spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q With all Israel listening, he said, \q "Sun, stand still at Gibeon! \q Moon, stand still in the valley of Aijalon!"

decisions.choice: be still: stop, stay where you are
decisions.reason: The verb means to be still or silent, to stop moving or stop acting (1 Samuel 14:9, "wait"; Psalm 4:5). Verse 13 takes it up with a second verb, "stood", so here it means that the sun should stop. Because the same verb can mean "be silent", some read it as a call for the sun to stop shining; see the note at verse 13.

decisions.choice: spoke to the LORD ... said in the sight of Israel: a prayer spoken as a command to sun and moon
decisions.reason: Joshua speaks to the LORD, yet his words are addressed to the sun and the moon, in front of all Israel. Verse 14 treats them as a request that the LORD heard: "the LORD listened to the voice of a man".

decisions.choice: at Gibeon ... in the valley of Aijalon: the sun to the east, the moon to the west
decisions.reason: Gibeon stands on the hills; the valley of Aijalon opens to the west of it, along the route of the flight (verses 10-11). The places named for the sun and the moon may say where Joshua saw them in the sky.

decisions.choice: the saying is a short poem
decisions.reason: The words to the sun and the moon, and the lines that follow in verse 13, are set in two matching lines each, as Hebrew poetry is. Verse 13 says they were written in the Book of Jashar.

decisions.choice: On the day the LORD handed the Amorites over ... Joshua spoke
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the time first. Readable says "gave ... victory over" for "gave ... before", and "with all Israel listening" for "in the sight of Israel".

records.heading: Sun, stand still at Gibeon

records.source: וַיִּדֹּ֨ם הַשֶּׁ֜מֶשׁ וְיָרֵ֣חַ עָמָ֗ד עַד־יִקֹּ֥ם גּוֹי֙ אֹֽיְבָ֔יו הֲלֹא־הִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל־סֵ֣פֶר הַיָּשָׁ֑ר וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹא־אָ֥ץ לָב֖וֹא כְּי֥וֹם תָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And was still the sun, and [the] moon stood, until took vengeance [the] nation [on] its enemies. [Is] it not written on [the] scroll of the Jashar? And stood the sun in [the] half of the heavens, and not hastened to go about a day complete.
pieces: So the sun stood still, and the moon halted, until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. \q Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? \q The sun stopped in the middle of the sky \q and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.

L.13: And the sun was still, and the moon stood, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. \q Is it not written in the Book of Jashar? \q And the sun stood in the middle of the heavens \q and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.

R.13: So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the people of Israel had paid back their enemies. \q This is written in the Book of Jashar, a book of old songs. \q The sun stopped in the middle of the sky. \q It waited about a whole day before it went down.

decisions.choice: what is described: daylight held on until the battle was won; how it happened is not said
alternatives: the sun's course was halted and the day made longer
the sun was silent: its heat or light was withheld
the sun and moon stood in positions read as a sign of victory
a poetic picture of a day of complete victory
decisions.reason: The poem says the sun "was still" and the moon "stood" until Israel had defeated its enemies. The prose that follows says the sun stood in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day, and verse 14 says no day was like it, because the LORD listened to a man. The text's own weight falls on God hearing Joshua and fighting for Israel; it does not explain how the day was lengthened. Readers have understood it in several ways: that the sun's course was truly halted and the day made longer; that "be still" means "be silent", so that the sun's heat or light was held back, perhaps by the storm of verse 11; that the sun and moon were seen in positions taken as a sign of victory; or that the poem's bold picture means a victory so complete that the day seemed to stretch out. The text itself does not decide between these.

decisions.choice: the Book of Jashar: a lost book, probably a collection of poems
decisions.reason: The name means "the book of the upright one". It is quoted again for David's lament over Saul and Jonathan (2 Samuel 1:18). Both quotations are poems about Israel's battles and heroes, so it seems to have been a collection of songs. No copy of it has survived. The question "Is it not written...?" points the reader to a source they could check.

decisions.choice: the quotation from the book: probably the poem of verses 12-13
alternatives: the book also contained the prose account of verses 13-14
decisions.reason: The question stands between the poem and the prose comment that follows, so it most likely refers to the lines to the sun and moon and their answer (verses 12-13). It is possible that the book also told the prose account that follows.

decisions.choice: until the nation took vengeance on its enemies: until Israel had defeated them
decisions.reason: "The nation" is Israel. To take vengeance here is to bring justice on enemies who attacked, by defeating them in battle.

decisions.choice: go (said of the sun): set
decisions.reason: The verb "go in" used of the sun means to set (verse 27; Genesis 15:12, 17).

decisions.choice: a book of old songs
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the Book of Jashar was, from what is known of it (m2), and turns the question "Is it not written...?" into a plain statement.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel had paid back their enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names the nation and uses plain words for taking vengeance (m4).

records.source: וְלֹ֨א הָיָ֜ה כַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לְפָנָ֣יו וְאַחֲרָ֔יו לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ יְהוָ֖ה בְּק֣וֹל אִ֑ישׁ כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה נִלְחָ֖ם לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And not was like the day the that before it and after it, for listening Yahweh to [the] voice of a man, for Yahweh fought for Israel.
pieces: No day before it or after it has been like it, a day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to a man's voice in this way. Truly {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} fought for Israel.

L.14: And there has been no day like that day, before it or after it, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to listen to the voice of a man, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} fought for Israel.

R.14: There has never been a day like it, before or since. On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did what a man asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to do, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was fighting for Israel.

decisions.choice: no day like it ... for the LORD to listen: what made the day unique was that God did what a man asked
decisions.reason: The phrase "for the LORD to listen" says in what way the day stood alone: the LORD granted a man's request to command the sun and moon. The length of the day is the sign of it.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice: heed, do what is asked
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to grant or obey what they say (Genesis 21:12; Numbers 21:3).

decisions.choice: the LORD fought for Israel: the promise kept
alternatives: because the LORD fought for Israel
decisions.reason: Moses said, "The LORD will fight for you" at the sea (Exodus 14:14) and before the conquest (Deuteronomy 1:30; 3:22). Verse 42 says it again. The word for ("for, because") may give the reason the day was unique, or may stand as a strong statement, "Truly the LORD fought..."; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Truly
decisions.reason: Balanced reads the last clause as a strong statement (m3); Literal keeps "for" and Readable "because", both of which it allows.

decisions.choice: did what a man asked him to do
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "listened to the voice of" (m2).

records.source: וַיָּ֤שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּֽלָה׃
records.gloss: And returned Joshua and all Israel with him to the camp at the Gilgal.
pieces: Then Joshua returned to the camp at Gilgal, and all Israel with him.

L.15: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

R.15: Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.

decisions.choice: Joshua returned to the camp at Gilgal: kept as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: leave the verse out, following the Greek
decisions.reason: The same sentence ends the chapter (verse 43). The ancient Greek translation does not have it here or in verse 43. Here it seems to come too early, since the story goes on at Makkedah and the army camps there (verse 21). It may close the account of the battle at Gibeon and the poem before the story turns back to the kings, telling in advance where the campaign ended. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence.

records.heading: The five kings in the cave at Makkedah

records.source: וַיָּנֻ֕סוּ חֲמֵ֖שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּחָבְא֥וּ בַמְּעָרָ֖ה בְּמַקֵּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And fled five the kings the these and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
pieces: Meanwhile the five kings had escaped and were hiding in the cave at Makkedah.

L.16: And these five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.

R.16: The five kings had run away and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.

decisions.choice: fled: during the battle, taking up the story from verse 11
decisions.reason: After the poem and the note on the day (verses 12-15), the story goes back to the flight of verse 11.

decisions.choice: the cave at Makkedah: a known cave
decisions.reason: The article marks a cave the readers knew; verse 27 says its stones were still there in the writer's day.

decisions.choice: Meanwhile ... had fled (Balanced), had run away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that this happened during the battle (m1).

records.source: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ לֵאמֹ֑ר נִמְצְאוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֔ים נֶחְבְּאִ֥ים בַּמְּעָרָ֖ה בְּמַקֵּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was told to Joshua, saying, Have been found five the kings hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
pieces: Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah."

L.17: And it was told to Joshua, saying, "The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Makkedah."

R.17: Someone told Joshua, "The five kings have been discovered! They are hiding in the cave at Makkedah."

decisions.choice: Someone told Joshua
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it was told to Joshua"; Readable makes it active.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ גֹּ֛לּוּ אֲבָנִ֥ים גְּדֹל֖וֹת אֶל־פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהַפְקִ֧ידוּ עָלֶ֛יהָ אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לְשָׁמְרָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua, Roll stones great to [the] mouth of the cave, and appoint over it men to guard them.
pieces: Joshua said, "Roll large stones over the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard the kings.

L.18: And Joshua said, "Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and appoint men over it to guard them.

R.18: Joshua said, "Roll big stones in front of the opening of the cave. Put some men there to guard the kings.

decisions.choice: appoint men over it to guard them: set a guard at the cave
decisions.reason: The verb means to put someone in charge. A few men were to keep the kings shut in while the rest pursued the enemy (verse 19).

decisions.choice: the kings
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "them"; Balanced and Readable say who is meant.

records.source: וְאַתֶּם֙ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֔דוּ רִדְפוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיכֶ֔ם וְזִנַּבְתֶּ֖ם אוֹתָ֑ם אַֽל־תִּתְּנ֗וּם לָבוֹא֙ אֶל־עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֧י נְתָנָ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, do not stand; pursue after your enemies and attack the rear of them; do not let them go into their cities, for has given them Yahweh your God into your hand.
pieces: But the rest of you, do not stop. Chase your enemies and cut down those at the rear. Do not let them reach their cities, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has handed them over to you."

L.19: But you, do not stand [still]. Pursue after your enemies and attack them from the rear. Do not let them go into their cities, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given them into your hand."

R.19: But the rest of you must not stop. Keep chasing your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them get back inside their cities. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has handed them over to you."

decisions.choice: attack them from the rear: cut down those at the back of the fleeing army
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for "tail" and is used again only in Deuteronomy 25:18, of Amalek attacking the stragglers at the back of Israel's march.

decisions.choice: their cities: the walled towns where they would be safe
decisions.reason: Once inside their walls, the survivors could hold out (verse 20); that is why Joshua wants them caught on the road.

decisions.choice: the rest of you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has an emphatic "you", set against the guards of verse 18; Balanced and Readable make the contrast plain.

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַכּוֹתָ֛ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה־מְאֹ֖ד עַד־תֻּמָּ֑ם וְהַשְּׂרִידִים֙ שָׂרְד֣וּ מֵהֶ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־עָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was, when finished Joshua and [the] sons of Israel striking them [a] striking great very until they were finished, and the survivors survived of them and went into [the] cities of the fortification,
pieces: When Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had finished striking them down in a very great slaughter, until they were wiped out, though a few survivors escaped into the fortified cities,

L.20: And it happened, when Joshua and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had finished striking them [with] a very great striking, until they were finished, and the survivors who survived of them had gone into the fortified cities,

R.20: Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated their enemies completely. They killed so many that the armies were wiped out. Only a few survivors escaped into their walled cities.

decisions.choice: until they were finished, and the survivors ... went into the cities: the armies were destroyed, though some escaped
decisions.reason: "Until they were finished" means the armies were destroyed as fighting forces. The next words say that some men still reached the walled towns, which Joshua then took one by one (verses 28-39).

decisions.choice: And it happened, when ...: the sentence runs on into verse 21
decisions.reason: Verse 20 sets the time; verse 21 tells what happened next.

decisions.choice: though a few
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two clauses with "though" to show how the destruction and the survivors fit together (m1).

records.source: וַיָּשֻׁבוּ֩ כָל־הָעָ֨ם אֶל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֧ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ מַקֵּדָ֖ה בְּשָׁל֑וֹם לֹֽא־חָרַ֞ץ לִבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְאִ֖ישׁ אֶת־לְשֹׁנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and returned all the people to the camp to Joshua [at] Makkedah in peace; not sharpened against [the] sons of Israel against a man his tongue.
pieces: the whole army came back safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah. No one dared to say a word against the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.21: then all the people returned to the camp, to Joshua at Makkedah, in peace. Not a man sharpened his tongue against the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.21: Then all the soldiers returned safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah. After that, no one dared to speak a word against the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: sharpened his tongue: spoke a threat, so much as moved the tongue against
decisions.reason: The same picture is used in Exodus 11:7, where not even a dog would growl at Israel. After the victory no one in the land dared to threaten Israel.

decisions.choice: in peace: safely, unharmed
decisions.reason: The army came back whole.

decisions.choice: the camp at Makkedah: a field camp
decisions.reason: During the campaign the army camped near the cave at Makkedah; the return to Gilgal comes at the end (verse 43; see the note at verse 15).

decisions.choice: the whole army (Balanced), all the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "All the people" here means the fighting men (verse 7).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ פִּתְח֖וּ אֶת־פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֗י אֶת־חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִן־הַמְּעָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua, Open [the] mouth of the cave and bring out to me five the kings the these from the cave.
pieces: Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring me those five kings."

L.22: And Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out to me these five kings from the cave."

R.22: Then Joshua said, "Open the cave and bring the five kings out to me."

decisions.choice: "from the cave" not repeated
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the cave twice; Balanced and Readable say it once.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עֲשׂוּ כֵ֔ן וַיֹּצִ֣יאוּ אֵלָ֗יו אֶת־חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִן־הַמְּעָרָ֑ה אֵ֣ת׀מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶת־מֶ֤לֶךְ חֶבְרוֹן֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ יַרְמ֔וּת אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ לָכִ֖ישׁ אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ עֶגְלֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And they did so, and brought out to him five the kings the these from the cave: king of Jerusalem, king of Hebron, king of Jarmuth, king of Lachish, king of Eglon.
pieces: They did so. They brought the five kings out of the cave to him: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.

L.23: And they did so, and they brought out to him these five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon.

R.23: So they brought the five kings out of the cave to Joshua. They were the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.

decisions.choice: the king of Jerusalem ... of Eglon: the five kings of verses 3 and 5
decisions.reason: The list repeats the five cities of verse 5, so that each king is named as he is brought out.

decisions.choice: to Joshua
decisions.reason: Readable names Joshua for "him".

records.source: וַ֠יְהִי כְּֽהוֹצִיאָ֞ם אֶת־הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵלֶּה֮ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֨א יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל־כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֶל־קְצִינֵ֞י אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הֶהָלְכ֣וּא אִתּ֔וֹ קִרְב֗וּ שִׂ֚ימוּ אֶת־רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם עַֽל־צַוְּארֵ֖י הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיִּקְרְב֔וּ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ אֶת־רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־צַוְּארֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, when they brought out the kings the these to Joshua, and called Joshua to every man of Israel, and said to [the] commanders of [the] men of the war who had gone with him, Come near; put your feet on [the] necks of the kings the these. And they came near and put their feet on their necks.
pieces: When they had brought these kings out to Joshua, he called for all the men of Israel. He told the commanders of the soldiers who had gone with him, "Come forward and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came forward and placed their feet on their necks.

L.24: And it happened, when they had brought out these kings to Joshua, that Joshua called for every man of Israel, and he said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come near; put your feet on the necks of these kings." And they came near and put their feet on their necks.

R.24: When the kings were brought to Joshua, he called all the men of Israel together. He said to the army commanders who had gone with him, "Come here. Put your feet on the necks of these kings." The commanders came forward and put their feet on the kings' necks.

decisions.choice: put your feet on the necks: a sign of complete victory
decisions.reason: A conqueror placing his foot on a defeated enemy showed that the enemy was wholly in his power (1 Kings 5:17; Psalm 110:1). Here it is done in front of all Israel, as a sign of what God will do (verse 25).

decisions.choice: commanders: officers who led the fighting men
decisions.reason: The word means a leader or chief, here the officers of the army.

decisions.choice: the commanders ... the kings' necks
decisions.reason: Readable names who came forward and whose necks are meant.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ אַל־תִּֽירְא֖וּ וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑תּוּ חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ כִּ֣י כָ֗כָה יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְכָל־אֹ֣יְבֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם נִלְחָמִ֥ים אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said to them Joshua, Do not fear and do not be dismayed; be strong and be bold, for thus will do Yahweh to all your enemies whom you [are] fighting them.
pieces: Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or discouraged. Be strong and courageous, because this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all the enemies you fight."

L.25: And Joshua said to them, "Do not fear, and do not be dismayed. Be strong and bold, for thus {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all your enemies whom you fight."

R.25: Joshua told them, "Do not be afraid. Do not lose heart. Be strong and brave. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all the enemies you fight against."

decisions.choice: do not fear ... be strong and bold: God's words to Joshua passed on to the army
decisions.reason: God gave Joshua this charge in 1:6, 7, 9 and said "Do not fear and do not be dismayed" in 8:1. Joshua now says the same to his commanders.

decisions.choice: thus the LORD will do: what was done to these kings is a sign of what is to come
decisions.reason: The kings under the commanders' feet show what will happen to every enemy Israel fights.

decisions.choice: bold (Literal), courageous (Balanced), brave (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:6.

records.source: וַיַּכֵּ֨ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ וַיְמִיתֵ֔ם וַיִּתְלֵ֕ם עַ֖ל חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה עֵצִ֑ים וַיִּֽהְי֛וּ תְּלוּיִ֥ם עַל־הָעֵצִ֖ים עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And struck them Joshua after so, and put them to death and hung them on five trees, and they were hanging on the trees until the evening.
pieces: After this Joshua struck them down and put them to death, and he hung them on five trees. They stayed hanging on the trees until evening.

L.26: And Joshua struck them afterward and put them to death, and he hung them on five trees, and they were hanging on the trees until the evening.

R.26: Then Joshua killed the kings and hung their bodies on five trees. They were left hanging there until evening.

decisions.choice: hung them on five trees: the dead bodies were displayed
decisions.reason: The kings were killed first and their bodies then hung up for all to see, as was done with the king of Ai (8:29). The word for "tree" can also mean a wooden post.

decisions.choice: their bodies
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the kings were already dead when they were hung up.

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י לְעֵ֣ת׀בּ֣וֹא הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ צִוָּ֤ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ וַיֹּֽרִידוּם֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָעֵצִ֔ים וַיַּ֨שְׁלִכֻ֔ם אֶל־הַמְּעָרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֶחְבְּאוּ־שָׁ֑ם וַיָּשִׂ֜מוּ אֲבָנִ֤ים גְּדֹלוֹת֙ עַל־פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֔ה עַד־עֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And it was, at [the] time of [the] going of the sun, commanded Joshua, and they took them down from on the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves there, and they put stones great on [the] mouth of the cave, until [the] very day the this.
pieces: At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took the bodies down from the trees and threw them into the cave where the kings had hidden. They placed large stones over the mouth of the cave, and they remain there to this very day.

L.27: And it happened at the time of the setting of the sun [that] Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves, and they put large stones over the mouth of the cave, until this very day.

R.27: When the sun was going down, Joshua gave orders. His men took the bodies down from the trees and threw them into the cave where the kings had hidden. They put big stones over the opening of the cave. Those stones are still there today.

decisions.choice: at sunset ... they took them down: the law of Deuteronomy 21:22-23
decisions.reason: The law said that a body hung on a tree must not stay there overnight. Joshua kept it here, as at Ai (8:29). On "the going of the sun" meaning sunset, see verse 13.

decisions.choice: until this very day: in the writer's own day
decisions.reason: The stones over the cave were still there when the book was written, as with the heap of stones over the king of Ai (8:29).

decisions.choice: the stones are there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what remained "until this very day".

records.source: וְאֶת־מַקֵּדָה֩ לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶרֶב֮ וְאֶת־מַלְכָּהּ֒ הֶחֱרִ֣ם אוֹתָ֗ם וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֨פֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖יר שָׂרִ֑יד וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מַקֵּדָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Makkedah captured Joshua on the day the that, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword, and its king; he devoted to destruction them and every person who [was] in it; not he left a survivor; and he did to [the] king of Makkedah just as he had done to [the] king of Jericho.
pieces: Joshua captured Makkedah that same day. He struck it down with the sword, together with its king, and devoted them to destruction with everyone in it. He left no survivors. He did to the king of Makkedah what he had done to the king of Jericho.

L.28: And Joshua captured Makkedah on that day, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king. He devoted them to destruction, and every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor. And he did to the king of Makkedah just as he had done to the king of Jericho.

R.28: That same day Joshua captured Makkedah. He struck it down with the sword, together with its king. He destroyed them completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with everyone in it. He left no one alive. He did to the king of Makkedah what he had done to the king of Jericho.

decisions.choice: devoted them to destruction: the town and its people were given over to God completely
decisions.reason: As in verse 1 and 6:17, 21. The command is given in Deuteronomy 7:2 and 20:16-17. "Them" means the king and the people of the town.

decisions.choice: with the mouth of the sword: by the sword, killing in battle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the sword's "mouth", the edge that "eats" (2 Samuel 2:26). The phrase means to kill with the sword, without sparing.

decisions.choice: as he had done to the king of Jericho: the pattern set at the first city
decisions.reason: Jericho and its king were given over to Joshua (6:2) and destroyed (6:21); Ai and its king followed the same pattern (8:2, 29). Verses 28-39 repeat the same words city after city.

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 1. Readable uses the same words for this term each time it appears in verses 28-40.

decisions.choice: the repeated phrases of verses 28-39 are worded the same each time
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a fixed set of phrases for each city taken ("struck it with the edge of the sword", "left no survivor", "did to its king as ..."). Each level keeps one wording for each phrase throughout, so the repetition can be heard. Balanced "left no survivors" is Readable "left no one alive". The move from town to town is worded the same way too: Literal "Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from ... to ...", Balanced "Next Joshua advanced from ... to ... with all Israel", Readable "Then Joshua and all Israel went on from ... to ...".

records.heading: The cities of the south are taken

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִמַּקֵּדָ֖ה לִבְנָ֑ה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עִם־לִבְנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And passed on Joshua and all Israel with him from Makkedah [to] Libnah, and fought with Libnah.
pieces: Next Joshua advanced from Makkedah to Libnah with all Israel and attacked Libnah.

L.29: And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Makkedah to Libnah, and he fought against Libnah.

R.29: Then Joshua and all Israel went on from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked Libnah.

decisions.choice: Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, Debir: the towns of the southern campaign
decisions.reason: From Makkedah the army moved through towns of the low hills to the southwest (Libnah, Lachish, Eglon), then turned up into the hill country (Hebron, Debir). The exact site of some of these towns is not certain.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה גַּם־אוֹתָ֜הּ בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לוְאֶת־מַלְכָּהּ֒ וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶ֗רֶב וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֨פֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֥יר בָּ֖הּ שָׂרִ֑יד וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לְמַלְכָּ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And gave Yahweh also it into [the] hand of Israel and its king, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword and every person who [was] in it; not he left in it a survivor; and he did to its king just as he had done to [the] king of Jericho.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed it and its king over to Israel as well. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it. He left no survivors. He did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.

L.30: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave it also, and its king, into the hand of Israel, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor in it. And he did to its king just as he had done to the king of Jericho.

R.30: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed it and its king over to Israel too. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it. He left no one alive. He did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.

decisions.choice: he struck it: Joshua, now the subject again
decisions.reason: The LORD gives the city into Israel's hand; Joshua and the army strike it. In verses 28-39 the Hebrew moves between "he" (Joshua) and "they" (Joshua and Israel) with no change in meaning.

decisions.choice: gave into the hand of Israel: handed over to Israel's power
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִלִּבְנָ֖ה לָכִ֑ישָׁה וַיִּ֣חַן עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And passed on Joshua and all Israel with him from Libnah to Lachish, and encamped against it and fought against it.
pieces: Next Joshua advanced from Libnah to Lachish with all Israel. He camped against it and attacked it.

L.31: And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Libnah to Lachish, and he camped against it and fought against it.

R.31: Then Joshua and all Israel went on from Libnah to Lachish. He camped around it and attacked it.

decisions.choice: camped against it: laid siege to the city
decisions.reason: The army set up camp before the walls in order to take the city (verse 5).

records.source: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־לָכִ֜ישׁ בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַֽיִּלְכְּדָהּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֑הּ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְלִבְנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And gave Yahweh Lachish into [the] hand of Israel, and he captured it on the day the second, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword and every person who [was] in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed Lachish over to Israel, and he captured it on the second day. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it, just as he had done to Libnah.

L.32: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who [was] in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.

R.32: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed Lachish over to Israel, and he captured it on the second day. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it, just as he had done to Libnah.

decisions.choice: on the second day: Lachish held out longer than the other towns
decisions.reason: Lachish was one of the strongest walled cities of the region. The other towns are taken "on that day" (verses 28, 35).

records.source: אָ֣ז עָלָ֗ה הֹרָם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גֶּ֔זֶר לַעְזֹ֖ר אֶת־לָכִ֑ישׁ וַיַּכֵּ֤הוּ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ וְאֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: Then came up Horam king of Gezer to help Lachish, and struck him Joshua and his people until not he left to him a survivor.
pieces: At that time Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his army, leaving him no survivors.

L.33: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people, until he did not leave him a survivor.

R.33: Then Horam, the king of Gezer, came to help Lachish. But Joshua defeated him and his army. He left no one alive.

decisions.choice: Horam king of Gezer: a king from the northwest
decisions.reason: Gezer lay to the northwest, on the edge of the low hills. Only its king and his army are said to be defeated; the town itself was not taken, and Canaanites still lived there later (16:10).

decisions.choice: his people: his army
decisions.reason: "People" often means the fighting men (verses 7, 21).

decisions.choice: defeated him and his army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "defeated" for "struck", since a king and his army in the field are meant, and "army" for "people" (m2).

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִלָּכִ֖ישׁ עֶגְלֹ֑נָה וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And passed on Joshua and all Israel with him from Lachish to Eglon, and they encamped against it and fought against it.
pieces: Next Joshua advanced from Lachish to Eglon with all Israel. They camped against it and attacked it.

L.34: And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Lachish to Eglon, and they camped against it and fought against it.

R.34: Then Joshua and all Israel went on from Lachish to Eglon. They camped around it and attacked it.

decisions.choice: they camped: Joshua and all Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 30: the Hebrew changes from "he" to "they" here without any change in meaning.

records.source: וַֽיִּלְכְּד֜וּהָ בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּהָ לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וְאֵת֙ כָּל־הַנֶּ֣פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא הֶחֱרִ֑ים כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְלָכִֽישׁ׃פ
records.gloss: And they captured it on the day the that, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword, and every person who [was] in it on the day the that he devoted to destruction, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
pieces: They captured it that same day and struck it down with the sword. He devoted everyone in it to destruction that day, just as he had done to Lachish.

L.35: And they captured it on that day, and they struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who [was] in it he devoted to destruction on that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

R.35: They captured it that same day and struck it down with the sword. That day he destroyed everyone in it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as he had done to Lachish.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַל יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מֵעֶגְל֖וֹנָה חֶבְר֑וֹנָה וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And went up Joshua and all Israel with him from Eglon to Hebron, and they fought against it.
pieces: Next Joshua went up from Eglon to Hebron with all Israel and attacked it.

L.36: And Joshua went up, and all Israel with him, from Eglon to Hebron, and they fought against it.

R.36: Then Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.

decisions.choice: went up: from the low hills into the hill country
decisions.reason: Hebron stands high in the hills of Judah, well above Eglon.

records.source: וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּהָ וַיַּכּֽוּהָ־לְפִי־חֶ֠רֶב וְאֶת־מַלְכָּ֨הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־עָרֶ֜יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ֙ לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֣יר שָׂרִ֔יד כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְעֶגְל֑וֹן וַיַּחֲרֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: And they captured it and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword, and its king and all its cities and every person who [was] in it; not he left a survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon; and he devoted to destruction it and every person who [was] in it.
pieces: They captured it and struck it down with the sword, together with its king, its towns and everyone in it. He left no survivors, just as he had done to Eglon. He devoted it to destruction with everyone in it.

L.37: And they captured it, and they struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king and all its towns and every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon. And he devoted it to destruction, and every person who [was] in it.

R.37: They captured it and struck it down with the sword, together with its king, the towns around it and everyone in it. He left no one alive, just as he had done to Eglon. He destroyed it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with everyone in it.

decisions.choice: its king: a king of Hebron after the one killed at Makkedah
alternatives: the repeated pattern, not a second king
decisions.reason: The king of Hebron was put to death at Makkedah (verses 23, 26). The king here may be one who had taken his place, or the phrase may follow the pattern of the other cities without naming a new king.

decisions.choice: all its cities: the smaller towns and villages that belonged to Hebron
decisions.reason: A main city ruled the towns of the land around it (15:44-45, "its towns and villages").

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

decisions.choice: the towns around it; destroyed ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what "its cities" were (m2) and explains the term as in verse 28.

records.source: וַיָּ֧שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֖וֹ דְּבִ֑רָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And returned Joshua and all Israel with him [to] Debir, and fought against it.
pieces: Next Joshua turned back to Debir with all Israel and attacked it.

L.38: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and he fought against it.

R.38: Then Joshua and all Israel turned back to Debir and attacked it.

decisions.choice: turned back to Debir: a town of the hill country, southwest of Hebron
decisions.reason: The army turned aside from Hebron to Debir, also called Kiriath-sepher (15:15). This is a town, not the king named Debir in verse 3.

records.source: וַֽיִּלְכְּדָ֞הּ וְאֶת־מַלְכָּ֤הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־עָרֶ֨יהָ֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּם לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וַֽיַּחֲרִ֨ימוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖יר שָׂרִ֑יד כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה לְחֶבְר֗וֹן כֵּן־עָשָׂ֤ה לִדְבִ֨רָה֙ וּלְמַלְכָּ֔הּ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לְלִבְנָ֖ה וּלְמַלְכָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And he captured it and its king and all its cities, and they struck them with [the] mouth of [the] sword and devoted to destruction every person who [was] in it; not he left a survivor; just as he had done to Hebron so he did to Debir and to its king, and just as he had done to Libnah and to its king.
pieces: He captured it, its king and all its towns. They struck them down with the sword and devoted everyone in it to destruction. He left no survivors. He did to Debir and its king what he had done to Hebron, and what he had done to Libnah and its king.

L.39: And he captured it and its king and all its towns, and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and they devoted to destruction every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor. Just as he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and to its king, and just as he had done to Libnah and to its king.

R.39: He captured it, its king and the towns around it. They struck them down with the sword and destroyed everyone in it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He left no one alive. He did to Debir and its king what he had done to Hebron, and what he had done to Libnah and its king.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

decisions.choice: all its cities: the towns that belonged to Debir
decisions.reason: As in verse 37.

decisions.choice: struck them (not "it")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "them" here, meaning the city, its king and its towns; each level keeps the plural, so the fixed phrase of verses 28-37 changes in this one word.

records.source: וַיַּכֶּ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֡רֶץ הָהָר֩ וְהַנֶּ֨גֶב וְהַשְּׁפֵלָ֜ה וְהָאֲשֵׁד֗וֹת וְאֵת֙ כָּל־מַלְכֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖יר שָׂרִ֑יד וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הַנְּשָׁמָה֙ הֶחֱרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ה יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And struck Joshua all the land, the hill country and the Negev and the Shephelah and the slopes, and all their kings; not he left a survivor, and every the breathing he devoted to destruction, just as had commanded Yahweh [the] God of Israel.
pieces: So Joshua struck the whole land: the hill country, the Negev, the foothills and the slopes, with all their kings. He left no survivors. He devoted to destruction everything that breathed, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel had commanded.

L.40: And Joshua struck all the land, the hill country and the Negev and the Shephelah and the slopes, and all their kings; he did not leave a survivor, and every breathing thing he devoted to destruction, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel had commanded.

R.40: So Joshua defeated the whole region: the hill country, the southern desert, the low hills in the west, and the slopes, with all their kings. He left no one alive. He destroyed every living person completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, had commanded.

decisions.choice: the hill country, the Negev, the Shephelah, the slopes: the regions of the south
decisions.reason: The hill country is the central ridge; the Negev the dry south; the Shephelah the low hills between the hills and the coastal plain (Deuteronomy 1:7). "The slopes" are the hillsides falling away from the ridge, toward the low hills or the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: every breathing thing he devoted to destruction, as the LORD commanded: the command of Deuteronomy 20:16-17
decisions.reason: Moses' law commanded that in the towns of the land Israel was to inherit, "you shall not leave alive anything that breathes" (Deuteronomy 20:16; 7:2). The verse says Joshua did as he was commanded.

decisions.choice: all the land: a summary of the campaign in sweeping terms
decisions.reason: The summary speaks of the whole region. The book itself shows that much land remained to be taken and some peoples remained in it (13:1-6; 15:63), and that the survivors of verse 20 escaped into their towns. The summary describes the decisive defeat of the kings of the south.

decisions.choice: the southern desert, the low hills in the west; destroyed ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable describes the regions instead of naming them, as in Deuteronomy 1:7, and explains the term as in verse 28.

records.source: וַיַּכֵּ֧ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ מִקָּדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵ֖עַ וְעַד־עַזָּ֑ה וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ גֹּ֖שֶׁן וְעַד־גִּבְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And struck them Joshua from Kadesh-barnea and as far as Gaza, and all [the] land of Goshen and as far as Gibeon.
pieces: Joshua struck them down from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and across the whole land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.

L.41: And Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea and as far as Gaza, and all the land of Goshen, and as far as Gibeon.

R.41: Joshua defeated them from Kadesh-barnea in the far south to Gaza near the coast, and from the region of Goshen up to Gibeon.

decisions.choice: from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, Goshen to Gibeon: the limits of the conquered region
decisions.reason: Kadesh-barnea lies in the far south, Gaza near the coast in the southwest, and Gibeon in the north where the battle began. This Goshen is a region in the south of Judah (11:16; 15:51), not the land of Goshen in Egypt (Genesis 45:10).

decisions.choice: in the far south ... near the coast
decisions.reason: Readable says where the places lie, so the reader can see the extent of the land.

records.source: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־הַמְּלָכִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ וְאֶת־אַרְצָ֔ם לָכַ֥ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ פַּ֣עַם אֶחָ֑ת כִּ֗י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נִלְחָ֖ם לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And all the kings the these and their land captured Joshua [at] time one, for Yahweh [the] God of Israel fought for Israel.
pieces: Joshua captured all these kings and their land in a single campaign, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel fought for Israel.

L.42: And all these kings and their land Joshua captured at one time, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel fought for Israel.

R.42: Joshua captured all these kings and their lands in one campaign, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, was fighting for Israel.

decisions.choice: at one time: in a single campaign
decisions.reason: The phrase means in one series of battles, not on one day. The northern campaign, by contrast, took "many days" (11:18).

decisions.choice: the LORD fought for Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 14.

decisions.choice: in a single campaign
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "at one time" (m1).

records.gloss: And returned Joshua and all Israel with him to the camp at the Gilgal.
pieces: Then Joshua returned to the camp at Gilgal, and all Israel with him.

L.43: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

R.43: Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.

decisions.choice: Joshua returned to the camp at Gilgal
decisions.reason: The same words as verse 15, where the evidence is described. Here they end the southern campaign; Gilgal remained Israel's base (14:6).
